strings.name: Germán Larrea
strings.role: Chairman and CEO of Grupo México
strings.summary: Germán Larrea is a Mexican business executive who has led Grupo México since 1994 and long chaired Southern Copper. His career spans mining, railways and energy; assessments of the group’s expansion must also consider its mines’ environmental impact and long-term remediation responsibilities.
strings.coverageNote: Reviewed through November 17, 2026. Birth sources differ in precision, so no definite date is entered. Subsidiary roles, group transactions and remediation plans are distinguished; corporate disputes are not presented as personal convictions.
strings.influence.rationale: Leads Grupo México’s mining and railway businesses, participating in North American copper production and logistics development.
strings.facts.f1.label: Distinct roles
strings.facts.f1.value: Has chaired Southern Copper since December 1999; served as its CEO from December 1999 to October 2004.
strings.facts.f2.label: Ownership scope
strings.facts.f2.value: Regulatory filings describe the Larrea family’s control of Grupo México voting rights through holding structures, not personal ownership of every share.
strings.highlights.h1.title: Managing multiple businesses
strings.highlights.h1.text: Has long been involved in mining and railways; the group also expanded its energy platform through a combination of power assets.
strings.highlights.h2.title: Environmental impact and remediation
strings.highlights.h2.text: The effects of the 2014 Sonora river basin pollution remain under scrutiny; in 2026, media still documented affected residents’ demands for remediation.
strings.timeline.t1.title: Sonora remediation progress reported
strings.timeline.t1.text: La Jornada reported the launch of a soil remediation programme; a year-end target and subsequent testing requirements did not mean cleanup was complete.
strings.timeline.t2.title: Discussed copper project progress
strings.timeline.t2.text: Commented as Southern Copper Chairman; Tía María was expected to begin operations in the first half of 2028, still a forward-looking plan.
strings.timeline.t3.title: Group power asset transaction closed
strings.timeline.t3.text: Saavi announced completion of its combination with Grupo México’s power assets; the group held 70% and GIP 30%.
strings.timeline.t4.title: Pollution spill at a group mine
strings.timeline.t4.text: Acidified copper sulfate from Buenavista del Cobre entered the Sonora and Bacanuchi river basins, with subsequent remediation disputed for years.
strings.timeline.t5.title: Became Southern Copper Chairman
strings.timeline.t5.text: Became Chairman and also CEO; his CEO tenure ended in October 2004.
strings.timeline.t6.title: Assumed railway leadership roles
strings.timeline.t6.text: Became Chairman and CEO of Grupo Ferroviario Mexicano.
strings.timeline.t7.title: Took the helm of Grupo México
strings.timeline.t7.text: Began serving as the group’s Chairman, President and CEO.
strings.timeline.t8.title: Joined the group’s Board
strings.timeline.t8.text: Became a director of Grupo México and subsequently served as Executive Vice Chairman.
